reply:
That's correct. My previous answer was wrong.

**Default Redis loses the last few minutes of writes on crash.** RDB snapshots every few minutes (e.g., `save 900 1`), and everything since the last snapshot evaporates if Redis dies. AOF with `appendfsync everysec` (the default) loses up to 1 second. Only `appendfsync always` gives you per-write durability, and it costs throughput.

The concrete cost of my error: someone building on that statement would ship unprotected data, lose production writes, and not know why.

Redis does not synchronously durably write by default. Data goes to memory, persistence happens separately on its own schedule.
